discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: Over two decades, pulsar timing arrays turned millisecond pulsars into a galaxy-sized gravitational-wave detector. In 2023 the NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA collaborations independently reported a common red-noise process with the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, the signature of a stochastic gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. This opened a new window, complementary to LIGO-Virgo and the future LISA, onto supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly early-universe physics such as first-order phase transitions and cosmic strings. McLaughlin was central to building NANOGrav and its long-term timing programme; Kramer led high-precision pulsar timing and the European array effort; Manchester founded the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array and shaped the methodology. The achievement is the result of long, patient, community-driven effort and rigorous statistical analysis, and it makes the gravitational-wave spectrum of the cosmos measurable across a new frequency band.
